purpose: Keep the historical house, diagrams, thumbnail and edits mechanically consistent.
house: Illustrative Seoul hanok c.1900; not a survey of Kim Chun-yeong's house.

canonical_geometry.courtyard: Main room rear right, maru rear left, lower kitchen right end, external chimney behind room.
canonical_geometry.cutaway: Side view: kitchen/firebox RIGHT, room LEFT above flues, far LEFT external chimney. The courtyard view is three-dimensional; use the same physical adjacency when changing viewpoint.

arrows.orange: Hot combustion gases BELOW sealed floor, then outside chimney.
arrows.amber: Heat through solid floor; not flowing smoke or water.
arrows.blue: Only ambient airflow around raised maru in summer graphic; never pipework in historical floor.

frames.S020: Occupied room, no numerical warmth guarantee

continuity.S064: Separate temple-cell example; never edit the household room into a claimed exact temple
continuity.S074: Early partial-floor comparison, no exact date or invention priority
continuity.S076: Modern water-pipe comparison, labelled and separate

wardrobe.indoor: Plain padded jeogori and baji; socks, no coat or outdoor shoes.
wardrobe.outdoor: Same base outfit under muted coat, simple dark shoes.
wardrobe.threshold: Use close-up transition or explicit shoe change; do not jump between incompatible full-body states.
wardrobe.summer: Visitor absent from summer comparison to avoid adding unnecessary summer costume generation.

historical_limits: No universal room temperature or fuel efficiency number.
Do not imply Seoul lacked electricity in c.1900.
Temple overheating is Bishop's separate experience; no exact temperature narrated.
Kim Chun-yeong house was originally in Samcheong-dong and moved in 1998; not a poor-family exemplar.
No paper over bare flame, smoke in room, red-hot floor, stove inside room or hot-water pipe in historical section.
execution: Build explanatory geometry locally as SVG/PNG stages, then composite labels. Inspect at full size and thumbnail size. Background illustrations show opaque finished architecture; never ask the image model to invent the internal engineering.
